F1: Post#cook` returns the feed HTML unsanitized for `raw_html` posts, and both the topic view and the embed view render it unescaped; `CGI.unescapeHTML` can turn escaped text inside CDATA into live markup, so outside content can run script on the forum origin.
F2: The URL goes into a single-quoted `href` with no escaping, and an anonymous `embed_url` on the embeddable host (for example one with a `'` in the query string) can add an attribute that survives into `cooked`, which is rendered raw.
F3: end if` followed by a newline is valid Ruby, because the parser carries the modifier `if` over to the next expression in the compiled ERB, so the template does not raise a SyntaxError.
F4: config/application.rb:61` does not list `embed.css` or `embed.js`, so in production, where assets are not compiled on demand, the stylesheet and the host-page script will fail to load.
F5: This is a robustness point: Sidekiq still logs the exception, and the unique-index race is a rare edge case.
F6: PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `@post` after a swallowed Rollback (for example, host-spam detection on a low-trust embed user with many same-host links), so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with a nil `post_id` and fails on the NOT NULL constraint.
F7: A separate throttle per distinct URL is how the feature is designed, and the gap between `setnx` and `expire` is a negligible edge case.
F8: cdn.host/x.png` passes `start_with?('/')`, and stripping the leading slashes rewrites it to the forum host, which breaks images and links.
F9: The handler only sets the iframe height, so the loose origin check has almost no impact.
F10: The thread `created_at` is still parsed (line 60) but no longer passed when the topic is created, so imported topics are dated at import time, after their own replies, which is wrong data.
F11: Rails 4 is the default and uses `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, which was updated; `Gemfile.lock` is only used when the `RAILS3` env var is set.
F12: Adding a column with a default is the normal migration pattern for this codebase, so the lock concern is generic operational hardening, not a defect.
